guardian.description:
Key regions of the brain linked to movement, learning and emotions were affected and may lead to cognitive problems

Babies born to mothers with anaemia have smaller brains, particularly in key regions linked to movement, learning and the regulation of emotion, according to a study.

Researchers said the differences, first detected at the age of one, could lead to cognitive problems when children started school.

france24fr.title: Cameroun : Maurice Kamto cède à la fronde et démissionne de la présidence du MRC
france24fr.description: L'opposant Maurice Kamto n'est plus président du parti Mouvement pour la Renaissance du Cameroun. Il a annoncé sa démission ce mardi, suite notamment à une fronde interne. Plus de détails avec notre correspondant, Marcel Amoko.

france24fr.title: Classement Pisa : comment enrayer la baisse du niveau des élèves ?
france24fr.description: L'enquête Pisa n'est plus seulement le classement de performances scolaires. Elle est devenue le révélateur d'un décrochage qui s'installe. Dans une grande partie des pays de l'OCDE, le niveau des élèves baisse. La France n'échappe pas à ce recul. Derrière les chiffres, une question se pose : pourquoi l'école peine-t-elle, année après année, à inverser la tendance ?

france24fr.title: Sénégal : la gestion de la dette, priorité du Premier ministre Lô devant l'Assemblée
france24fr.description: Le Premier ministre sénégalais Ahmadou Al Aminou Lô a fait ce mardi sa déclaration de politique générale devant le parlement. Une assemblée acquise en majorité au Pastef d'Ousmane Sonko, son prédécesseur. Lô a évoqué l'accord avec le FMI promet de redresser l'économie du Sénégal, mais parle de sacrifices. Un ajustement structurel a même été évoqué. Précisions du correspondant de France 24 à Dakar, Élimane Ndao.

france24fr.title: Xénophobie au Kenya, l'inquiétude des Burundais grandit
france24fr.description: Au Kenya, la xénophobie est en train de prendre racine. Depuis les déclarations du président Ruto ce lundi 7 septembre, stigmatisant les travailleurs étrangers, les Burundais manifestent leur colère. Ils sont 16 000 réfugiés et demandeurs d’asile burundais à vivre au Kenya, et beaucoup survivent grâce à des emplois dans le secteur informel. À présent, la très grande majorité n’ose plus travailler et cherche désormais à quitter le territoire.

france24fr.title: Moyen-Orient : l’Iran riposte après des frappes américaines
france24fr.description: Les Gardiens de la Révolution, armée idéologique de l'Iran, ont dit mercredi avoir attaqué une base militaire des Etats-Unis en Jordanie ainsi qu'une vingtaine de bateaux dans le Golfe, en réponse à des frappes américaines contre des pétroliers iraniens.

france24fr.title: À Paris, l'Europe tente de rattraper SpaceX et les États-Unis
france24fr.description: Il a été voulu par le président Emmanuel Macron lui-même : le sommet de l'Espace s'ouvre ce mercredi à Paris. L’objectif : tenter de contrecarrer les hégémonies américaine et chinoise dans le domaine. Mais les Européens ont pour le moment bien du mal à se coordonner… Récit de Jules Boiteau.

france24fr.title: Guerre au Moyen-Orient : l'armée américaine détruit "5 pétroliers iraniens"
france24fr.description: Les Gardiens de la révolution iranienne disent avoir attaqué des pétroliers liés à Washington. Téhéran promet des représailles "plus dures" si les États-Unis continuent leurs attaques. En riposte, l'armée américaine a revendiqué des frappes contre cinq tankers coulés dans le détroit d'Ormuz.

france24fr.title: Une frappe russe à la frontière moldave, des drones ukrainiens ciblent une base militaire en mer Noire
france24fr.description: L'Ukraine a été visée mercredi par une attaque de drones russes qui a fait au moins deux morts et plusieurs blessés près de la frontière moldave. De son côté, Moscou a dit avoir abattu près de 600 drones ukrainiens dans la nuit de mardi à mercredi, qui visaient notamment une base militaire dans une ville portuaire de la mer Noire, faisant état d'au moins quatre morts et de nombreux blessés.

france24fr.title: Donald Trump et Vladimir Poutine échangent au téléphone à propos de l'Ukraine
france24fr.description: Quelques heures après le bruit des bombes à Kiev, Vladimir Poutine et Donald Trump se sont entretenus au téléphone. Le Kremlin a salué une conversation d’une "extrême franchise" à propos de l'Ukraine. Les frappes russes sur Kiev ce mardi ont fait au moins 5 morts et 25 blessés. De son côté, le président Volodymyr Zelensky espère une reprise des pourparlers entre Moscou, Kiev et Washington dès ce mois-ci. Précisions d’Olivier Faissolle.

france24fr.title: Éliminatoires de la CAN 2027 : des sélections contraintes à l'exil faute de stade
france24fr.description: Dans un peu plus de deux semaines, l'Afrique lance les éliminatoires de la CAN 2027, où 48 sélections se disputent un billet pour le Kenya, l'Ouganda et la Tanzanie. Mais selon la CAF, 14 pays ne disposent d'aucun stade homologué, et 21 n'en ont qu'un seul. Des sélections comme le Lesotho, la Namibie, la Centrafrique ou le Zimbabwe se voient interdire de jouer devant leur public. Le Maroc (16 stades) et l'Afrique du Sud (13 stades) servent donc souvent de solutions de repli. Décryptage de Benoît

france24fr.title: Netanyahu était au courant des attaques du 7-Octobre, révèle Haaretz
france24fr.description: En Israël, les élections législatives ont lieu le mois prochain. Benjamin Netanyahu, très critiqué, tente de rassembler la droite et l'extrême droite pour se maintenir au pouvoir. Mais un scandale vient d'éclater : le journal de gauche Haaretz révèle que le Premier ministre aurait été directement averti des attaques du 7-Octobre quelques jours avant et n'aurait rien fait. Explications d’Olivier Faissolle.

france24fr.title: Quelle réaction israélienne aux sanctions de douze pays contre la colonies israéliennes ?
france24fr.description: Douze pays, dont la France et le Royaume-Uni, vont imposer des restrictions de commerce sur les biens issus de colonies israéliennes en Cisjordanie occupée. L’annonce survient suite à une explosion des violences de colons ​contre les Palestiniens. Explications de Florent Rodo.

france24fr.title: Colombie : les États-Unis en tournée pour "renouer" les liens
france24fr.description: Les États-Unis veulent resserrer les liens avec la Colombie, l'Équateur our encore le Pérou. Ces derniers mois, plusieurs pays d'Amérique du Sud ont élu des présidents ouvertement pro-Trump. Le secrétaire d'État des États-Unis Marco Rubio prévoit ainsi de conforter l'influence de Washington dans la région. Un décryptage de Gauthier Rybinski, chroniqueur international France 24.

france24fr.title: Ouverture d'un sommet international sur l'espace à Paris sur fond de rivalité franco-allemande
france24fr.description: Le sommet international sur l'espace s'ouvre au Grand Palais, à Paris, sans SpaceX, Blue Origin ni le chancelier allemand Friedrich Merz. Derrière ces absences se joue une autre bataille : celle des nouveaux lanceurs européens, où la France et l'Allemagne sont désormais autant concurrentes que partenaires.

france24fr.title: Albanie : la "révolution des flamants roses" contre Trump continue
france24fr.description: Les Albanais continuent de se mobiliser contre le luxueux projet immobilier de Jared Kushner, gendre de Donald trump, dans une zone naturelle protégée d'Albanie. Devant l'Assemblée nationale, les habitants manifestent en continu depuis 101 jours. Un important dispositif policier a été mis en place et plusieurs personnes ont été interpellées par les forces de l'ordre.

france24fr.title: L'Arabie saoudite riposte et mène une quarantaine de frappes au Yémen
france24fr.description: Le Yémen est à son tour entraîné dans la guerre au Moyen-Orient. Les rebelles houthis intensifient leurs attaques contre l'armée régulière yéménite, mais aussi contre son principal soutien, l'Arabie Saoudite. Une escalade condamnée par l'Union européenne et les Nations unies. Précisions de Nicolas Chamontin.

france24fr.title: L'Iran riposte à des frappes iraniennes et attaque une base militaire en Jordanie
france24fr.description: Les Gardiens de la Révolution iranienne annoncent mercredi avoir mené des frappes en Jordanie. La veille, les États-Unis avaient détruit cinq pétroliers iraniens. La reprise des échanges de tirs depuis une semaine a interrompu ‌un mois de calme relatif dans le conflit. Les négociations restent au point mort. Récit de Nicolas Chamontin.

phys-org.title: Q&A: What can rent prices reveal about inflation and the economy?

phys-org.title: OpenAI says 10,000 AI agents cracked one of math's hardest problems in 88 hours

This tendency was associated with a greater willingness to make ethical compromises for money or status, as well as to accept immoral help when it benefited them.

phys-org.description: Ocean color remote sensing is a vital tool for monitoring global ocean carbon sinks and primary productivity. However, the on-orbit calibration accuracy of satellite sensors is insufficient, and weak marine signals account for only approximately 10% of the signals received by satellites, leading to significant uncertainties in ocean color remote-sensing applications.

phys-org.title: New computational method pushes cryo-electron microscopy beyond traditional resolution limits

I was on the hunt for a yellow-rumped warbler—a bird affectionately called "butter-butt" by birdwatchers after the distinctive buttery yellow patch of feathers above its tail.

phys-org.description: Since the 1950s, the Tibetan Plateau has experienced pronounced warming and wetting. However, an overall shift toward wetter conditions does not necessarily mean that drought risk has diminished. On the contrary, against the backdrop of continued warming, compound hot-dry events—characterized by the simultaneous occurrence of high temperatures and drought—have become an increasingly important climate risk across the plateau.

phys-org.title: Some black holes grow much faster than their galaxies

That's because galaxies and their black holes have formed hand in hand. There is still some debate as to whether galaxies formed around the seeds of supermassive black holes or the other way around, but there is plenty of evidence to support the idea that the two evolve together.

undark.title: Book Review: The Messy Business of Making Science Happen

How did science miss these benefits? The answer, he says, lies in our inability to do things in moderation.

undark.title: The New Student Visa Policy Doesn’t Add Up
undark.description: In July, the Department of Homeland Security issued new rules that would make it harder for international students to complete their studies in the U.S. The policy threatens to be disruptive for students — particularly doctoral candidates — and self-defeating for the country.

undark.title: Book Review: How Wildlife Is Returning to the East
undark.description: In “The Beasts of the East,” journalist Andrew Moore charts the natural history of the East and the people who have dedicated their careers to restoring several long lost species to what remains of their original habitats.

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain
undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

undark.title: Interview: How Tragedy Changed the FDA
undark.description: As an FDA advisory committee prepares to weigh whether specialized pharmacies should be allowed to dispense seven unapproved peptides, Mikkael A. Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?

But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

proj-syn.title: The BRICS at 20
proj-syn.description: If the promise of the BRICS was to establish a monetary union, a single market, or a tightly integrated political alliance, it has not been fulfilled. But if it was to build a platform for emerging economies to cooperate while advancing their own strategic autonomy, the BRICS has exceeded expectations.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Security Depends on a Clear Electrification Target
proj-syn.description: The politics around electrification are beginning to shift in Europe as more people recognize its importance for economic competitiveness and industrial resilience. European Union policymakers should seize this momentum to embed a binding target of at least 50% electrification by 2040 in the bloc’s energy security framework.

proj-syn.title: The AI Race Could Sink US-China Détente
proj-syn.description: The competition between the United States and China to develop AI and deploy it globally poses the biggest threat to the two countries’ currently constructive relations. Without an ongoing AI dialogue to avoid escalation, a return to the zero-sum conflict that rattled both sides last year cannot be ruled out.

proj-syn.title: Are China’s Rare Earths Really a Potent Weapon?
proj-syn.description: The available evidence indicates that Chinese rare-earth export restrictions would cost the West far less than often feared, though this cost is impossible to estimate precisely in advance. This is forcing prudence on both sides, to the disappointment of geopolitical hawks and the benefit of the global economy.

proj-syn.title: The Trump Shock in East Asia
proj-syn.description: US President Donald Trump has alarmed his East Asian allies by canceling two joint military exercises with South Korea, a move that seems motivated less by whim than by a fondness for tyrants. The question now is whether South Korea and Japan will set aside historical resentments for the sake of mutual interests.

proj-syn.title: Building a Resilient Nepal
proj-syn.description: After Japan’s 2011 Fukushima nuclear disaster, the Japanese government changed the building codes for schools and housing and rethought the placement of critical infrastructure. Nepal (and other vulnerable countries) must pursue a similar approach.

proj-syn.title: Unpaid Work in the AI Age
proj-syn.description: Unpaid work, such as dealing with government bureaucracy and private-sector administration, consumes a huge amount of people's free time. While AI tools have the potential to change this, with important implications for the economy, predictions about AI’s impact tend to focus exclusively on paid work.

proj-syn.title: The Digital Wellness Industry Is Hijacking Women’s Health
proj-syn.description: Menopause and perimenopause, long under-researched and dismissed, have become a growth industry for online advertisers and wellness companies. Mining intimate data, this lucrative digital ecosystem exploits medical uncertainty to sell women hormones and supplements they don't need, or that can even harm them.

proj-syn.title: Who Controls the Data Controls the Future
proj-syn.description: While AI is becoming increasingly central to finance, defense, health care, and public administration, it depends on resources most governments do not control: the data used to train it and the compute that processes it. Unless this changes, countries will remain subject to decisions made in boardrooms they cannot influence.

proj-syn.title: Will Europe Be as Unprepared as Ukraine Was?
proj-syn.description: With Russia ramping up its hybrid war, Europe must choose. It can invest in its own defense, accept the trade-offs involved, and build credible deterrence, or it can continue to underspend, hope that diplomacy will suffice, assume that US protection will always be available, and tell itself that the war in Ukraine is a local affair.

proj-syn.title: The Case for a Cashflow Tax
proj-syn.description: In the context of the US economy, a cashflow tax would offer far-reaching benefits in promoting economic growth, taxing rents, and raising incremental revenue efficiently. Moreover, well-known concerns about complexity and fairness are easily addressed.

proj-syn.title: Kevin Warsh’s Best Move Is to Do Nothing
proj-syn.description: Beholden to mainstream economic ideas, the new US Federal Reserve chair has committed himself, and his reputation, to a goal he cannot achieve. Reining in inflation requires not interest-rate adjustments but much larger strategic shifts that are not within the Fed’s power to influence.

proj-syn.title: How Developing Countries Can Do More With Less
proj-syn.description: Evaluation frameworks for development projects have long been influenced by donor priorities. But foreign-aid cuts have created an opportunity for African countries to implement equitable evaluation practices, both to channel limited resources more effectively and to shape the future of global development governance.

proj-syn.title: America’s Naval Disaster
proj-syn.description: Plagued by exorbitant costs and chronic delays, American shipbuilders cannot produce enough vessels to keep pace with China. US President Donald Trump’s push to rebuild the industry does little to address its underlying problems and threatens to squander hundreds of billions of dollars.

proj-syn.title: America’s Un-American AI Companies
proj-syn.description: The United States can prevail in the AI race against China by leaning into the strengths of an open society: democratic oversight, the rule of law, robust competition, and open public debate. But that won’t happen as long as American AI companies aggressively lobby against accountability and cozy up to the state.

proj-syn.title: The Golden Bridge to Monetary Multipolarity
proj-syn.description: Gold has overtaken US Treasuries as the world’s top reserve asset because it offers a solution to the challenges of a rogue America. But its renewed relevance also reflects how rapid technological diffusion and increasing dispersion of economic power are creating a more diversified international monetary system.

proj-syn.title: Asia’s Natural Disasters Must Not Become Financial Crises
proj-syn.description: The dangerous flooding in Nepal and Tibet has demonstrated, once again, the need for prearranged disaster-risk financing to prepare for the economic chain reactions triggered by natural disasters. Asia’s policymakers must act now to help cash-strapped Nepal and strengthen other countries’ resilience before the next crisis hits.

proj-syn.title: Is AI Crowding Out Other Investment?
proj-syn.description: The AI investment boom has unleashed a wave of demand for capital just as savings are declining and interest rates remain high. As competition for financing intensifies, rising borrowing costs could squeeze non-AI firms looking to finance new factories, equipment, and projects.
